test_title: RRB Group D Previous Year Paper (Held on: 5 Sept 2022 Shift 2)
subject: general
question: A dealer buys two articles X and Y at ₹600 each. He marks the same price on each of them. He sells X at two successive discounts of 25% and 15%, and still makes a profit of ₹216. If he sells Y at a single discount of 46%, find the percentage profit he makes on Y.
solution:
**Given:**

Cost price of article X = ₹600

Cost price of article Y = ₹600

Profit on article X = ₹216

Two successive discounts on article X = 25% and 15%

Single discount on article Y = 46%

**Formula Used:**

Selling Price (SP) = Cost Price (CP) + Profit

Marked Price (MP) = SP / (1 - Discount%)

Profit Percentage = (Profit / Cost Price) × 100

**Calculation:**

For article X:

Selling Price (SP) of X = ₹600 + ₹216 = ₹816

Let the Marked Price (MP) be M.
